summary: A CCC-era 100-foot Aermotor lookout in Graham County on the Coronado NF; NRHP-listed and NHLR-registered 2003. The 1933 significant year and the 1934 date for CCC structures conflict; staffing unverified.

facts.design: 100-foot Aermotor MC-39 tower with a 7 x 7 ft steel cab, plus a log cabin ground house

events.note: NRHP record gives 1933 as the significant year, not as the tower build year; it lists the CCC under architects
NHLR dates the related CCC structures to 1934, which differs from the 1933 NRHP year; no source read gives the tower build year

evidence.supports: 100-foot Aermotor MC-39 tower with a 7x7 steel cab
evidence.quote: Heliograph Lookout is a 100’ Aermotor MC-39 tower with a 7’x7’ steel cab.

evidence.supports: still in active service; tallest tower on the Coronado National Forest
evidence.quote: Still in active service and the tallest tower on the Coronado National Forest

evidence.supports: log cabin ground house and CCC structures dated 1934

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NRHP record gives 1933 as the significant year, while the NHLR page dates the related CCC structures to 1934. The story reports both years and does not pick one.

notes_for_editor: Staffing and access are not established by any source read; the NHLR page says only 'still in active service' with no date, so no staffing or access key is recorded. The NRHP nomination PDF (npgallery GetAsset) timed out and the Living New Deal page returned 403, so the 1933 significant year rests on the NRIS asset page alone, and no source read gives a build year for the tower. A Living New Deal search snippet said 1933 but was not read directly and is not cited. Brief elevation 3046.5 m matches NHLR 3,046 m. Verification pass (2026-10-08) relabelled the 1933 and 1934 events from built to other, because neither source gives the tower build year, and added a second-source footnote.
